headline: Bottled soybean oil supply shrinks again as companies push for price hike
summary: Bottled soybean oil is scarce in markets, with open soybean and palm oil prices rising by Tk 2-4 per liter. Egg prices have also increased, adding to the burden of already high broiler chicken and fish costs.
details: The supply of bottled soybean oil has decreased again in the market. Simultaneously, the prices of open soybean and palm oil have increased by Tk 2-4 per liter in the past week. Farmed chicken egg prices have also seen a slight rise.

Retailers report that companies are releasing smaller quantities of bottled soybean oil into the market, leading to reduced supply from dealers. Dealers have informed them that companies are aiming to increase oil prices, which is why they have reduced supply.

Market observations reveal that retail shops are not receiving adequate supplies of 1, 2, and 5-liter soybean oil bottles to meet demand. In some areas, specific bottle sizes are entirely unavailable, with many shops having only a few bottles in stock.

When bottled soybean oil supply is scarce, the demand and price for open soybean oil typically increase. According to the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB), open soybean oil prices rose by nearly 1% in the last week, reaching Tk 190-195 per liter. Open palm oil prices also increased by 0.88% to Tk 170-175.

This marks the third instance of a soybean oil supply crisis this year, following similar shortages in February and July. Previous shortages led to price adjustments, with the price per liter increasing to Tk 199 in late April and then to Tk 204 on September 3.

Edible oil refining and producing companies in the country are seeking another increase in soybean oil prices. The Bangladesh Vegetable Oil Refiners and Vegetable Fat Manufacturers Association sent a letter to the Commerce Secretary regarding this on September 20.

However, Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir stated that the government would make a decision after careful consideration and verification. He assured that edible oil prices would not be increased without proper assessment.
In the past week, egg prices have risen by approximately Tk 10 per dozen, now costing Tk 155-160 per dozen. For low-income families, purchasing a single egg now costs Tk 15.

Additionally, broiler chicken prices have remained high, around Tk 200 per kg, for the past two months. Various types of fish also continue to be expensive, further straining the budgets of low and limited-income individuals.

headline_marked: [[Qawmi teacher accused of beating student, breaking leg]] in Meherpur
headline: Qawmi teacher accused of beating student, breaking leg in Meherpur
summary: A 13-year-old student at Fazlul Ulum Qawmi Madrasa in Gangni, Meherpur, sustained a fractured ankle after allegedly being beaten by his teacher for not completing his studies. He is currently receiving treatment at the Upazila Health Complex.
details: A 13-year-old student, Shouyeb Ali, at Fazlul Ulum Qawmi Madrasa in Gangni, Meherpur, has allegedly had his leg broken by his teacher, Deen Islam. Shouyeb, son of Abdul Ghani from West Malshadah village, was studying in the Hifz section of the madrasa.
According to Shouyeb, the teacher, Deen Islam, beat him with a bamboo stick because he failed to recite his lessons. The beating resulted in injuries to various parts of his body.
Shouyeb's father, Abdul Ghani, initially did not realize the severity of the injury. However, when his son was unable to walk, he took him to Gangni Upazila Health Complex on Thursday afternoon.

At the health complex, doctors examined Shouyeb and confirmed a fracture in his ankle bone. Dr. Samia Sultana, Medical Officer, stated that the student is currently receiving treatment at the hospital.

Attempts to contact the teachers of West Malshadah Fazlul Ulum Qawmi Madrasa by phone for comment were unsuccessful. The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Gangni Police Station, Muhaddid Morshed Chowdhury, stated that necessary action would be taken upon receipt of a written complaint regarding the incident.
